name: Pseudo-Labeling
analogy: Think of it as a junior analyst who studies a small stack of graded exam bars, then grades the ungraded pile himself. He trusts only the answers he feels sure about, adds those to his study stack, and studies again.

steps.title: Train on the labelled bars
steps.description: The model first learns from the bars with a known outcome, exactly as an ordinary supervised model would. This first version is weak because there are few labels.
steps.inExample: A neural network is trained on 300 five-minute MNQ bars with a known outcome 6 bars later.

steps.title: Score the unlabelled bars
steps.description: The model is run over all the bars with no known outcome and gives each a probability. Nothing is checked at this point, because no answers exist for these bars.
steps.inExample: All 6,000 unlabelled bars get a probability of closing higher.

steps.title: Keep only the confident answers
steps.description: Only bars where the model is clearly leaning one way are kept, using a confidence cut-off. The rest are left unlabelled. The cut-off protects the model from learning its own guesses where it was really unsure.
steps.inExample: A bar is kept if its probability is at least 62 percent or at most 38 percent. In round one, 410 bars pass.

steps.title: Treat the kept answers as labels
steps.description: The model's own confident calls become pseudo-labels, meaning labels that are guesses, and are added to the training set. Often they count for less than real labels at first.
steps.inExample: The 410 bars are added with their predicted side, up or down, as the label, at half the weight of a real label.

steps.title: Retrain and repeat
steps.description: The model is trained again on the real labels and the pseudo-labels together, then scores the remaining unlabelled bars again. Each round can add more bars, and the dividing line is refined as it does.
steps.inExample: Round two adds 360 bars and round three adds 380, so 1,150 bars carry pseudo-labels at the end.

steps.title: Check on later bars and score new ones
steps.description: The final model is checked on real-labelled bars from a later period that never entered training. If the pseudo-labels have taught it noise, this check shows it. New bars are then scored as usual.
steps.inExample: The 14:30 bar is scored at 61 percent for closing higher.

useFor.example: Training a direction model on MNQ 5-minute bars when only 300 bars have clean outcome labels and thousands more have none.

useFor.task: A semi-supervised step on any probability model
useFor.example: Wrapping an existing neural network or gradient boosting run in a pseudo-labelling loop without changing the model itself.
Classifying candlestick patterns from chart images when only a few hundred images were labelled by hand.
Listing the bars that never pass the confidence cut-off, which are the ones the model cannot separate.

avoidWhen: Price direction is close to a coin flip, so few answers are truly confident and the confident ones may simply be noise the model fits; the model then teaches itself its own errors.
Your first model is weak or poorly calibrated; its confident calls are then unreliable and the loop amplifies them. Use a Calibrated Classifier first, or choose a graph-based method.

example.scenario: A researcher has 6,300 five-minute MNQ bars, 300 with a known outcome: whether the close 6 bars (30 minutes) later was above that bar's close. After three rounds of pseudo-labelling, the model scores the 14:30 bar.

input.summary: Labelled and unlabelled bars, the confidence cut-offs, and the features of the bar to score.

fields.name: labelled bars
fields.meaning: Bars with a known outcome that start the process.

fields.name: unlabelled bars
fields.meaning: Bars with no outcome that supply the pseudo-labels.

fields.name: confidence cut-offs
fields.meaning: A bar is kept only if its probability is at or above 62 or at or below 38 percent.

fields.name: rounds
fields.meaning: How many times the score-keep-retrain cycle runs.

fields.name: price change over the last 6 bars
fields.meaning: How far price fell over the previous 30 minutes before the 14:30 bar.

fields.name: volume against its 20-bar average
fields.meaning: How heavy trading was compared with the recent norm; here more than double the usual.

fields.name: average true range, 14 bars
fields.meaning: The typical high-to-low travel of a recent five-minute bar.

output.summary: A probability for the 14:30 bar and how many pseudo-labels the final model rests on.

fields.name: probability the close is higher 6 bars later
fields.meaning: The final model's answer for the 14:30 bar.

fields.name: call
fields.meaning: The side the probability falls on when the dividing line is 50 percent.

fields.name: bars carrying pseudo-labels
fields.meaning: How many unlabelled bars became training rows over the three rounds.

example.reading: 61 percent is a lean, and it rests partly on guessed labels, so verify it on real-labelled bars from a later month before trusting it. If its accuracy there is no better than the model trained on 300 labels alone, the pseudo-labels added nothing.
